title: All praise is His, here and in the Hereafter.
subtitle: The Owner of everything is the One to thank
then: Saba opens in Makkah, at a time when the Prophet's message ﷺ was met with mockery and taunts. It begins with praise. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}all praise is His because He is the Giver{/idea} to the people of this world and the next, and He will be praised for eternity.
now: You get the promotion, pass the exam, close the deal. The first words out of your mouth are about how hard you worked. {idea}All of it, the effort included, was His gift.{/idea} Alhamdulillah is the true first word.
old: When something good happens, it is mainly because of what I did.
new: Everything belongs to Allah, so the praise for every good thing is His.
try: The next time something goes well today, say Alhamdulillah before you say anything else.

title: He knows every raindrop that sinks and every deed that rises.
subtitle: Nothing moves unseen by Him
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah knows {idea}the number of raindrops that sink into the earth and the seeds that are sown{/idea}, and what comes down from the sky and what rises to it, including {reward}righteous deeds{/reward}. He is Merciful and does not rush to punish, and forgives those who repent.
now: You helped someone carry groceries. You said a quiet dua for a stranger in the hospital waiting room. Nobody saw. {reward}Every one of those rose to Him{/reward}, known as surely as each drop of rain.
old: My small, unseen good deeds probably do not count for much.
new: Allah knows every deed that rises to Him, however small or hidden.
try: Do one small good deed today that no one will ever know about.

title: Yes, by my Lord, it will come. Not an atom escapes Him.
subtitle: One of three verses with this oath
then: Ibn Kathir says this is one of only three verses where the Prophet ﷺ is told to {idea}swear by his Lord that the Hour will come{/idea}, against stubborn denial. Even when bones scatter and decay, {idea}Allah knows where every piece has gone{/idea} and will bring them back.
now: You think about how big the world is and how small you are. Billions of people, endless data. Surely your little choices get lost. {idea}Not an atom's weight escapes Him.{/idea} Nothing you do is lost in the crowd.
old: In a world this big, my choices disappear in the noise.
new: Not even an atom's weight escapes Allah. Every choice of mine is recorded.
try: Notice one tiny choice today, like a word or a glance, and make it a good one on purpose.

title: The Hour comes so good deeds are finally rewarded.
subtitle: Why there must be a Day
then: After swearing that the Hour will come, Allah gives the reason: {reward}to reward those who believe and do good with forgiveness and noble provision{/reward}. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse saying the people of the Fire and of Paradise are not equal.
now: You played fair at work and someone who cheated got the bonus. You stayed honest on your taxes and a friend laughed at you. It feels like good goes nowhere. {reward}The Hour exists so that nothing good is wasted.{/reward}
old: Doing good often seems to get me nothing in return.
new: The Day is coming so every good deed is repaid with forgiveness and provision.
try: Do one honest thing today that costs you a little, and leave the reward to Allah.

title: Working to defeat Allah's signs is a race you cannot win.
subtitle: Those who try to block the message
then: Ibn Kathir explains these are {trap}those who try to turn others away from the path of Allah{/trap} and reject His Messengers. They hoped to make His signs fail. The verse is a sober warning: the effort turns against the one making it.
now: Sometimes the one fighting a reminder is you. You argue against a verse because following it would cost you. You look for reasons it does not apply. {idea}Fighting the signs never defeats them.{/idea} It only wears you out.
old: If I find enough arguments, I do not have to follow this verse.
new: Struggling against Allah's signs only harms me. Surrender is lighter.
try: Pick one verse you have been arguing with inside. Read it slowly today without arguing back.

title: Those with knowledge see it is the truth.
subtitle: Knowledge that leads to recognition
then: Ibn Kathir says when believers see the Hour arrive and the reward unfold as their Books described, they will say {idea}the Messengers of our Lord came with the truth{/idea}. Knowledge here is not trivia. It is {reward}recognizing the path to the Mighty and Praiseworthy{/reward}.
now: You can know dozens of facts about the Quran from videos and podcasts and still not feel it guide your day. {idea}Real knowledge is when you see the truth and it changes your direction.{/idea}
old: The more facts I collect, the more knowledge I have.
new: Knowledge is seeing the truth clearly and letting it guide where I go.
try: Take one fact you already know about Islam and act on it today.

title: Shall we show you the man who says dust lives again?
subtitle: Mocking what you cannot imagine
then: The disbelievers of Makkah {trap}mocked the Prophet ﷺ for speaking of the Hour{/trap}, pointing to him as the man who claims bodies scattered into dust will be made new. Ibn Kathir says they thought he was either lying or deluded.
now: You hear someone laugh at belief in life after death as old-fashioned. You feel a little embarrassed for believing it. {idea}Mockery is not an argument.{/idea} The One who made you from nothing can make you again.
old: If something sounds strange to modern ears, maybe it is not true.
new: Mockery proves nothing. The Creator who began it can bring it back.
try: Next time you feel shy about a belief, quietly remind yourself why you hold it.

title: Liar or mad? Neither. The far error is theirs.
subtitle: The labels turned back on those who used them
then: They said the Prophet ﷺ was either {trap}inventing a lie against Allah or mad{/trap}. Allah answered: those who disbelieve in the Hereafter are the ones in torment and far error. Ibn Kathir says {idea}Muhammad ﷺ is the one telling the truth, righteous and wise{/idea}.
now: You hear a hard truth from a friend, and your first move is to label them: judgmental, extreme, crazy. {trap}Labeling the messenger is easier than hearing the message.{/trap} {idea}Ask whether the words are true.{/idea}
old: If the person telling me a hard truth seems odd, I can ignore it.
new: Labeling the one who warns me does not change whether the warning is true.
try: Think of advice you dismissed because of who said it. Weigh the words alone today.

title: Sky above, earth below: a sign for whoever turns back.
subtitle: Sky above, earth below, wherever you go
then: Ibn Kathir explains: wherever they go, the sky is above and the earth beneath. If Allah wished, He could act against them, {idea}but He delays because He is Patient and Forgiving{/idea}. The One who built the heavens can raise bodies again, {reward}a sign for every servant who turns to Him{/reward}.
now: You walk out of the office at dusk and the sky is huge and orange. For a second the deadlines shrink. {idea}That second is a sign meant for you{/idea}, for the person who is ready to turn back.
old: The sky and the earth are just the background of my life.
new: The sky above and earth below are signs pointing me back to Allah.
try: Step outside today and look up for one full minute. Think of the One who built it.

title: Mountains and birds praised with Dawud, and iron softened.
subtitle: Gifts given to a grateful prophet
then: Saba's introduction contrasts Dawud and Sulayman, who stayed grateful despite great power, with the people of Saba, who grew proud. Dawud had {reward}a voice so beautiful the mountains and birds repeated Allah's praise with him{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ once heard Abu Musa reciting and said he had been given one of the melodies of Dawud's family.
now: You have a talent: a good voice, quick hands, a way with words. The world tells you to monetize it, show it off. {idea}Dawud's gift was used to praise Allah, and creation joined in.{/idea}
old: My talents are mine to use for my own name.
new: My gifts are from Allah, and they shine brightest when used to praise Him.
try: Use one skill you have today for Allah's sake, even something small like reciting beautifully.

title: Make it well, measure it right, and do good.
subtitle: Craft done carefully, under Allah's sight

row.title: measure the links
sub: not too loose, not too tight

then: Qatadah said Dawud was the first to make chain mail. Mujahid explained the instruction: {idea}do not make the rings too loose so they rattle, or too tight so they cannot move, but just right{/idea}. Then: work righteousness, for {reward}Allah sees all you do{/reward}.
now: You are fixing a bug, plastering a wall, writing a report. Nobody will check the details. {idea}Allah taught a prophet to get the size of each ring right.{/idea} Careful, balanced work is part of doing good.
old: As long as the job gets done, the details do not matter much.
new: Doing my work carefully and in balance is a kind of righteousness.
try: Pick one task today and do the part nobody will check just as well as the rest.

title: The wind, the copper, and the jinn worked by Allah's permission.
subtitle: Power given to Sulayman, and its limits
then: After Dawud, Allah mentions his son Sulayman. The wind carried him a month's journey in a morning and another by evening, and {reward}a spring of copper flowed for him{/reward}. The jinn worked for him, but Ibn Kathir stresses it was {idea}by Allah's decree and permission{/idea}.
now: You run a team, manage a budget, have influence in your circle. People do what you ask. {idea}All of it works by Allah's permission.{/idea} The moment you forget that, the power starts to own you.
old: The influence I have is something I built myself.
new: Every power I hold works only by Allah's permission.
try: Before you give an instruction to anyone today, remind yourself it is by Allah's leave.

title: Work in gratitude, family of Dawud. Few are grateful.
subtitle: Thanks shown in deeds, not only words
then: The jinn built palaces, basins like reservoirs, and fixed cauldrons. Then the command: {idea}work, family of Dawud, in gratitude{/idea}. Al-Hubuli said prayer, fasting, and every good deed are thanks. Dawud asked how he could thank Allah when thanks itself is a gift, and was told: {reward}now you have truly thanked Me{/reward}.
now: You are blessed with a home, health, a phone in your hand. You say thank God now and then. {idea}This verse asks for thanks you can see: in how you pray, give, and treat people.{/idea} Few do it. You can be among the few.
old: Saying thank you to Allah with my tongue is enough.
new: Gratitude is work. Every good deed I do is a way of saying thanks.
try: Turn one blessing you have into a deed today, like giving from your food or time.

title: A tiny worm revealed what the jinn never knew.
subtitle: The death of Sulayman and the limits of the unseen
then: Sulayman died leaning on his staff, and stayed that way a long time while the jinn kept working. Only when {idea}a small creature of the earth ate through the staff{/idea} and he fell did they realize. Ibn Kathir says it became clear {trap}the jinn do not know the unseen, as they had led people to believe{/trap}.
now: Horoscope apps, palm readers, someone who claims to see your future. It is tempting when you are anxious about money or marriage. {idea}The jinn could not even tell that a king had died in front of them.{/idea} The unseen is Allah's alone.
old: Someone with special insight might be able to tell me what is coming.
new: Only Allah knows the unseen. I bring my worries about the future to Him.
try: When you feel anxious about the future today, make a short dua instead of searching for answers.

title: A good land and a forgiving Lord. Just eat and give thanks.
subtitle: The two gardens of Saba
then: Saba were the people of Yemen, living behind the great dam of Ma'arib. Qatadah said a woman could walk under the trees with a basket on her head and {reward}it would fill with falling fruit{/reward}. They were told: {idea}eat from your Lord's provision and be grateful. A good land, and a forgiving Lord.{/idea}
now: A full fridge. Clean water from the tap. A safe street to walk on at night. You barely notice them. {idea}The only thing asked in return is gratitude and worship.{/idea} It is a small price for a good land.
old: The comforts I have are just normal, not something to thank anyone for.
new: Every comfort is provision from my Lord, given with an invitation to thank Him.
try: Before your next meal, name three blessings around you and thank Allah for each.

title: They turned away, and the dam broke.
subtitle: From fruit gardens to bitter scrub
then: Ibn Kathir says the people of Saba followed the message for as long as Allah willed, then {trap}turned away from worship and thanks{/trap}. They were sent a flood from the dam that scattered them. {trap}Their two gardens became bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote trees.{/trap}
now: You built something solid: savings, a business, a strong body. You feel safe behind it like a wall. {idea}No wall holds when gratitude is gone.{/idea} The blessing and its protection both come from Allah.
old: What I have built is strong enough to protect me.
new: Blessings are protected by gratitude to Allah, not by the walls I build.
try: Thank Allah today for one thing you usually take for granted as safe and permanent.

title: Only the ungrateful are repaid like this.
subtitle: The law behind Saba's loss
then: Allah says plainly why Saba lost everything: {trap}because they were ungrateful and disbelieved{/trap}. The verse asks: does He repay this way except the ungrateful? The introduction to Saba sets this against Dawud and Sulayman, who had even more and {reward}stayed grateful{/reward}.
now: Ingratitude is quiet. It is a sigh at the dinner table, a complaint about the car that works fine, a shrug at your health. {idea}It is the start of turning away.{/idea} Gratitude keeps you on the other side of this verse.
old: Complaining about what I have is harmless venting.
new: Ingratitude is a turning away. Thankfulness keeps me among the grateful.
try: Catch one complaint before it leaves your mouth today and replace it with a thanks.

title: Towns all along the road, safe by night and day.
subtitle: The easy trade route of Saba
then: Ibn Kathir says Saba traveled from Yemen to Sham through {reward}towns joined to one another{/reward}. They needed to carry no food or water. They could rest at noon in one town and spend the night in another, {reward}safe both by night and by day{/reward}.
now: Your commute has cafés, gas stations, and phone signal the whole way. You can drive at midnight without fear. {reward}That is a gift most people in history never had.{/reward}
old: Safe roads and easy travel are just how things are.
new: Safety and ease on the road are gifts from Allah, worth thanking Him for.
try: On your next trip, say the travel dua and thank Allah for the safety of the road.

title: They asked for hardship and became a story told at night.
subtitle: Bored with ease, scattered like Saba
then: Ibn 'Abbas and others said Saba {trap}grew tired of the easy road and wanted long journeys through empty wilderness{/trap}. They were scattered so widely that Arabs would say: scattered like Saba. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}the believer's affair is all good: grateful in ease, patient in hardship{/reward}.
now: Life is fine, and it bores you. You want something dramatic, a change, a risk, a fight. {trap}Restlessness with blessing can be its own ingratitude.{/trap} {idea}Being grateful when life is quiet is a skill.{/idea}
old: When life is easy and calm, it feels boring and I want more.
new: A calm, easy life is a blessing to thank Allah for, not to escape.
try: On a quiet moment today, instead of reaching for stimulation, simply say Alhamdulillah.

title: Iblis guessed most would follow him, and he was right.
subtitle: Except a group of believers

row.title: Iblis
sub: you will not find most thankful

then: After Saba, Allah speaks of all who follow Iblis and their desires. Ibn 'Abbas linked this to Iblis's vow: {trap}I will come at them from front and back, right and left, and You will not find most of them thankful{/trap}. His guess came true, {reward}except for a group of believers{/reward}.
now: Everyone at work pads their hours. Everyone in your class shares answers. Following the crowd feels normal. {trap}That is exactly what Iblis predicted.{/trap} {idea}The verse names an exception, and you can be in it.{/idea}
old: If most people do it, it must be normal and fine.
new: Iblis bet on most people. I want to be in the group that proves him wrong.
try: Notice one thing you do only because everyone does it. Do the opposite once today.

title: Shaytan has no real authority, only a test.
subtitle: Whispers that reveal who believes
then: Ibn 'Abbas said Iblis {trap}had no proof over them{/trap}. He was allowed to whisper only to {idea}make clear who believes in the Hereafter and who doubts it{/idea}. Ibn Kathir adds that by Allah's watching and care, the believers who follow the Messengers are saved.
now: You slip, and you blame the devil, the mood, the late night. Shaytan whispered, yes. {idea}But he has no power to force you.{/idea} Every whisper is a question, and you give the answer.
old: When I give in to temptation, it is because Shaytan is too strong.
new: Shaytan only whispers. The choice is mine, and Allah guards those who turn to Him.
try: Next time a bad urge comes, say a'udhu billah and pause ten seconds before acting.

title: Call on them: they do not own an atom's weight.
subtitle: The emptiness of other gods
then: Allah challenges the idol worshippers of Makkah: {idea}call on those you claim besides Allah{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains that they possess nothing, alone or as partners, and Allah needs no support from any of them. {trap}All creation is in need of Him.{/trap}
now: Your lucky charm, your boss's approval, the stock market, a famous person whose word you trust. When panic hits, you call on one of them first. {idea}None of them owns an atom's weight.{/idea}
old: Some people and things in my life can really save me.
new: Nothing besides Allah owns even an atom. My first call goes to Him.
try: When you feel worried today, make your first move a dua before any phone call.

title: Even the angels tremble at His word, and repeat it exactly.
subtitle: Intercession only by His permission
then: No one can intercede with Allah unless He permits. The Prophet ﷺ said when Allah decrees a matter, {idea}the angels beat their wings in submission, like a chain on smooth rock{/idea}. When the awe lifts they ask, what did your Lord say, and answer: the truth. Even the greatest intercessor ﷺ will first prostrate and wait to be told to speak.
now: You hope someone will put in a good word for you: a parent, a sheikh, a saint. {idea}Even the angels tremble before His word.{/idea} Intercession is His gift to give. The safest path is to turn to Him directly.
old: If I have the right connections, they can speak for me before Allah.
new: Intercession is only by Allah's permission. I turn to Him myself.
try: Make one dua today directly to Allah, without asking anyone else to pray for you first.

title: Allah feeds you from sky and earth, so one side is wrong.
subtitle: Not both paths can be right
then: The Makkans admitted that Allah sends rain and grows crops. Ibn Kathir explains the next step: {idea}then He alone deserves worship{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ is told to say that {idea}either we or you are on guidance or in clear error{/idea}. Both cannot be right.
now: You keep two lives: one at the masjid, one with friends who mock it. You tell yourself both are fine. {idea}The verse asks you gently to check the proof and choose.{/idea}
old: I can keep one foot on each path without choosing.
new: If Allah provides everything, then worship belongs to Him alone.
try: Name one area of your life where you are avoiding a clear choice. Decide one step today.

title: You will not answer for our sins, nor we for yours.
subtitle: Each answers for their own deeds
then: Ibn Kathir says this line separates the two sides after the call has been made. The Prophet ﷺ invited them to worship Allah alone. If they refused, {idea}each side would answer for its own actions{/idea}. He links it to the surah that says: to you your religion, and to me mine.
now: You spend energy on what your sibling, your colleague, your neighbor is doing wrong. You know their sins better than yours. {idea}You will be asked about your own deeds, not theirs.{/idea}
old: Watching what others do wrong is part of being religious.
new: I will answer for my deeds. My energy is better spent on my own record.
try: When you notice someone else's fault today, use it as a cue to check one of your own.

title: He will gather us and judge between us with truth.
subtitle: Al-Fattah, the One who opens the verdict
then: Ibn Kathir explains that on the Day of Resurrection Allah will {idea}bring all creation together in one arena and judge with justice{/idea}. Each will be repaid by their deeds, and then everyone will know who truly succeeded. He is Al-Fattah, the Judge who knows the true state of every affair.
now: An old family dispute never got resolved. You still replay the argument in the shower. {idea}There is a Judge who knows the whole story{/idea}, every side of it. You can let the case rest with Him.
old: Unless I win this argument now, justice will never be done.
new: Allah will judge between us with truth. I can let the case rest with Him.
try: Think of one argument you keep replaying. Say: Allah will judge between us. Then let it go.

title: Show me these partners. No, He alone is Allah.
subtitle: The challenge that no one can meet
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say: {idea}show me those you attached to Him as partners{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains the answer: {trap}no{/trap}, He has no peer, rival, or equal. He is Allah, {reward}the Almighty, the All-Wise{/reward}, wise in all His words, laws, and decrees.
now: Your career sits in His place some days. Your image, your income, the person you love. Ask yourself the verse's question: {idea}show me what this thing actually controls.{/idea} The answer brings things back to size.
old: Some things in my life are so important they feel like everything.
new: Nothing shares Allah's place. Asking what it really controls puts it in perspective.
try: Pick the thing that worries you most today and ask: what does this actually control?

title: Sent to all people, though most do not know.
subtitle: A message with no borders
then: The Prophet ﷺ said earlier prophets were sent to their own people, but {idea}he was sent to all of mankind{/idea}. Qatadah said he was sent to Arabs and non-Arabs, and {reward}the most honored with Allah is the most obedient{/reward}. The verse adds that most people do not know.
now: Your coworker from another country, the delivery driver, the neighbor who never asked about Islam. {idea}The message was sent to them too.{/idea} Your kindness may be the first they see of it.
old: Islam is mainly for people from my background.
new: The message was sent to everyone. Honor with Allah is by obedience, not origin.
try: Be especially kind today to someone from a very different background than yours.

title: When is this promise? they ask, as if mocking delays it.
subtitle: Rushing what you do not believe in
then: The Makkans thought the Hour was unlikely and taunted: {trap}when is this promise, if you are truthful?{/trap} Ibn Kathir links it to the verse saying {trap}those who do not believe want to hurry it{/trap}, while {idea}believers are wary of it and know it is the truth{/idea}.
now: A friend jokes: if Judgment Day is real, why has it not come yet? You laugh along. {idea}The delay is not a sign it is false.{/idea} It is time given to get ready.
old: If the Day were really coming, it would have come by now.
new: The delay is mercy and time to prepare, not proof that it is not real.
try: Use one moment of free time today as if it were borrowed time before the Day.

title: Your appointment is fixed, not an hour early or late.
subtitle: A date no one can move
then: Allah answers the taunt: {idea}you have an appointment for a Day{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says it is fixed and cannot be changed, {trap}not put back an hour or brought forward{/trap}. He links it to the verse: when Allah's term comes, it cannot be delayed.
now: Your calendar is full of things you can reschedule. Meetings, dentist, catch-up calls. You treat repentance the same way: maybe next Ramadan. {trap}This is the one appointment you cannot move.{/trap}
old: I can always push the serious things to a later date.
new: My appointment with Allah is fixed. I prepare now, not later.
try: Take one good intention you keep postponing and put it on today's list.

title: If not for you, we would have believed.
subtitle: Followers and leaders blaming each other
then: The deniers said they would never believe in the Quran or what came before it. Allah describes them later {trap}throwing blame back and forth{/trap} before their Lord. The followers say to their leaders: {trap}if not for you, we would have believed{/trap}.
now: You tell yourself: if my parents had taught me, if my friends were better, I would pray. Maybe there is some truth. {idea}But the verse shows that blame does not save anyone there.{/idea} You can still choose here.
old: If the people around me were better, I would be a better Muslim.
new: Blaming others will not help me on that Day. I can choose my path now.
try: Name one thing you blame others for not teaching you. Learn one small part of it today.

title: Did we block you from guidance? No, you chose this.
subtitle: The leaders push the blame back
then: The leaders reply: {trap}did we keep you from guidance after it came to you?{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains their words: we only called you, and {idea}you followed without any proof, against the proof the Messengers brought{/idea}. It was your own choice.
now: A friend talked you into skipping prayers for a party. Later he says: I did not force you. He is partly right. {idea}Guidance was there, and you walked past it.{/idea} Owning that is the first step back.
old: If someone else pressured me, the fault is entirely theirs.
new: Guidance was in front of me. I answer for choosing to follow someone else.
try: Admit to yourself one choice you blamed on pressure. Ask Allah's forgiveness for your part.

title: Your plotting night and day misled us, they say.
subtitle: Both sides hide their regret
then: The followers answer: {trap}it was your plotting night and day{/trap}, tempting us with promises and telling us we were rightly guided. Ibn Kathir says {trap}both the leaders and the followers will feel regret{/trap}, and each will be repaid according to what they did.
now: A feed that works on you night and day. Ads, influencers, endless videos that tell you what success looks like. {trap}The plotting is constant.{/trap} {idea}You can step out of it a little each day.{/idea}
old: The voices around me shape me so much that I cannot help it.
new: Constant influence is real, but I still answer for my choices. I can step back.
try: Mute or unfollow one account today that keeps pulling you away from Allah.

title: Every warner was rejected first by the comfortable.
subtitle: Why luxury makes the truth hard to hear
then: Allah consoles the Prophet ﷺ: no warner was sent to a town except that {trap}its people of luxury said, we reject what you bring{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}the weaker people tended to follow the Messengers{/idea}, as with Nuh and Salih. Qatadah called the wealthy rejecters their tyrants and leaders in evil.
now: When your life is comfortable, warnings feel like they are for someone else. You have a good salary, a nice flat, a full schedule. {trap}Comfort quietly lowers the volume on guidance.{/trap} {idea}Listen hardest when life is easy.{/idea}
old: When life is going well, I do not really need warnings.
new: Comfort can make me deaf to truth. I listen more carefully when life is easy.
try: On a good day this week, deliberately listen to a reminder you would usually skip.

title: We have more money and children, so we will be fine.
subtitle: Mistaking blessings for approval
then: The wealthy rejecters said {trap}we have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says they thought their riches were a sign that Allah loved them. He links it to the verse asking: do they think the wealth and sons We give them are Us hurrying good to them? {idea}They do not perceive.{/idea}
now: Business is booming, the kids are doing well, the house is paid off. A quiet thought: I must be doing something right with Allah. {trap}Blessings are not a certificate of approval.{/trap} {idea}They are a test of what you do with them.{/idea}
old: If I have plenty, it must mean Allah is pleased with me.
new: Wealth and children are a test, not proof that Allah is pleased with me.
try: Look at one blessing you have and ask: what am I doing with this for Allah?

title: He widens and narrows provision, and most do not understand.
subtitle: Rich and poor by His wisdom
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to answer: {idea}my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says He gives wealth to those He loves and those He does not love, and makes poor whom He wills. {trap}Most people do not understand this.{/trap}
now: Your cousin is rich and careless. You pray and struggle to pay rent. It stings. {idea}Your bank balance is not Allah's opinion of you.{/idea} He gives and holds back by wisdom you cannot fully see.
old: If I were closer to Allah, I would be richer than I am.
new: Allah widens and narrows provision by His wisdom. It is not a measure of my worth.
try: When you compare your income to someone else's today, say: my Lord knows best. Then stop.

title: Not wealth or children brings you near, only faith and good deeds.
subtitle: What Allah looks at
then: The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth, but at your hearts and your deeds{/idea}. Only faith and good deeds bring a person near. Ibn Kathir says their reward is multiplied, and {reward}they live in the high rooms of Paradise, safe from all fear{/reward}.
now: You scroll profiles full of cars, holidays, and perfect families. You feel small. {idea}None of it is what Allah looks at.{/idea} A quiet good deed today counts for more than any of it.
old: Money, looks, and a good family make someone important.
new: Allah looks at my heart and deeds. Faith and good work bring me near.
try: Do one good deed today that nobody can see and that costs you something.

title: Those who work to defeat His signs are brought to account.
subtitle: The other side of the high rooms
then: Right after the believers in the high rooms, Allah mentions {trap}those who strive against His signs, trying to make them fail{/trap}. The two verses sit side by side: {idea}the same energy can build a place in Paradise or work against the truth{/idea}.
now: You spend hours arguing online, trying to win, trying to tear down. {idea}The same hours could go into learning, helping, building.{/idea} Effort is never neutral. It is always pointed somewhere.
old: Arguing and tearing things down is just how I express myself.
new: My effort always goes somewhere. I want it pointed toward good, not against it.
try: Take the time you would spend arguing today and spend it learning one verse.

title: Whatever you spend, He replaces it. He is the best Provider.
subtitle: Giving does not shrink what you have
then: Allah repeats that He widens and narrows provision, this time for {idea}His own servants{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says He does so by a wisdom no one else can grasp. Then the promise: {reward}whatever you spend, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers{/reward}.
now: Payday. Rent, bills, groceries, and a donation link someone shared. You hesitate: I need this more right now. {reward}The verse says giving is replaced by the best Provider.{/reward} It does not vanish.
old: Every bit I give away is money I will never see again.
new: What I spend for Allah is replaced by Him. The best Provider does not lose.
try: Give a small amount to someone in need today, even a coin, and trust the promise.

title: Were these people worshipping you? Allah asks the angels.
subtitle: The question on the Day of gathering
then: Ibn Kathir says some idolators claimed their idols were in the form of angels who would bring them closer to Allah. On the Day, Allah will ask the angels: {idea}was it you these people worshipped?{/idea} He likens it to when 'Isa is asked whether he told people to worship him.
now: You say you do it for Allah: the volunteering, the charity post, the long prayer. But part of you is doing it for the likes, the praise, the image. {idea}One day the question will be asked out loud: who were you really doing it for?{/idea}
old: As long as I say it is for Allah, it counts as for Allah.
new: The truth of who I serve will be made clear. I want my intention clean now.
try: Before one good deed today, pause and quietly fix your intention for Allah alone.

title: Glory be to You. We have nothing to do with them.
subtitle: The angels disown those who worshipped them
then: The angels answer: {idea}Glory be to You, You are our Protector, not them{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they disown the idolators before Allah. In truth those people {trap}served the devils who made idol worship attractive to them{/trap}. Most of them believed in them.
now: You lean on a person, a group, a cause, sure they will stand by you no matter what. {trap}Even the angels will step away from those who worshipped them.{/trap} {idea}Only Allah is a Protector who never disowns you.{/idea}
old: The people I give my loyalty to will always stand by me.
new: Only Allah is a true Protector. Everyone else will be busy with themselves.
try: Say today: You are my Protector, ya Allah. Mean it about one worry you carry.

title: That Day, no one can help or harm anyone else.
subtitle: When every borrowed hope runs out
then: After the angels disown those who worshipped them, Allah says: {trap}today none of you can benefit or harm one another{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains that the rivals they hoped would help them in hard times {trap}will have no power at all{/trap}. The wrongdoers are reminded of the Fire they used to deny.
now: You keep a list in your head of people who will rescue you: a rich uncle, a well-connected friend, a good lawyer. {idea}Sincere reliance on Allah now is the only plan that still works then.{/idea}
old: There will always be someone who can bail me out.
new: On that Day no one can help or harm another. I rely on Allah now.
try: Think of your biggest worry. Hand it to Allah in a dua before you plan anything else.

title: He wants to take you from your fathers' ways, they said.
subtitle: Three labels to avoid listening
then: When clear verses were recited to them, {idea}fresh from the lips of the Messenger ﷺ{/idea}, they answered with labels: {trap}a man who wants to turn you from your fathers' worship, an invented lie, plain magic{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says they assumed their fathers' religion was the truth.
now: Your family does something a certain way because it has always been done. You read a verse that says otherwise. The first reaction: but this is how we do it. {idea}Old is not the same as true.{/idea}
old: If my family has always done it this way, it must be right.
new: Tradition is precious, but it is right only when it matches the truth.
try: Pick one family habit and ask honestly: is this from Allah, or just from us?

title: They wished for a book and a warner, then rejected both.
subtitle: The first scripture they ever received
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah sent no book and no prophet to the Arabs before the Quran and Muhammad ﷺ. {idea}They used to say: if only a warner came to us, we would be more guided than others.{/idea} {trap}When it came, they rejected it.{/trap}
now: You said if only you had more time, you would read Quran. Then lockdown came, or a long holiday. You said if only you had a good teacher. Then one moved next door. {idea}Notice when your wish has already been answered.{/idea}
old: If I only had the right conditions, I would be much more religious.
new: Often what I wished for has already come. The question is whether I take it.
try: Name one thing you once wished for to help your faith. Use it today if you already have it.

title: Those before had ten times the power and still fell.
subtitle: Strength did not save the nations of old
then: Ibn 'Abbas said the Makkans had {trap}not even a tenth of the worldly power{/trap} given to earlier nations. Those nations had hearing, sight, and hearts, and more numbers and strength. {trap}None of it protected them when they denied the Messengers.{/trap}
now: You see a huge company, a celebrity, a powerful family, and think: they will never fall. History is full of giants that did. {idea}Your own strength is even smaller.{/idea} Only obedience to Allah lasts.
old: Being strong and well-resourced keeps me safe.
new: Strength never saved anyone who turned from the truth. Obedience does.
try: Read about one past nation in the Quran this week and note what brought them down.

title: Just one thing: stand for Allah, in pairs or alone, and think.
subtitle: Honest reflection, away from the crowd
then: To those who called him mad, the Prophet ﷺ asked one thing: {idea}stand before Allah sincerely, in pairs or alone, without desire or tribal loyalty, and think{/idea}. He had once climbed As-Safa and asked Quraysh if they would believe him warning of an enemy. They said yes. He said: {trap}I am a warner to you before a severe punishment{/trap}.
now: Your opinions about faith are shaped by group chats, comment sections, and what your friends think. {idea}Turn it all off for ten minutes.{/idea} Sit alone, or with one honest friend, and think it through for yourself.
old: I mostly know what I think from what people around me think.
new: Truth is clearer when I stand for Allah alone or with one friend and reflect.
try: Spend ten quiet minutes today, phone away, thinking honestly about one question of faith.

title: Keep any payment. My reward is with Allah.
subtitle: Advice given with nothing to gain
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to say: {idea}I want nothing from you for conveying the message{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains: I seek my reward from Allah, who knows everything about me, how I convey it, and about you.
now: You help a younger colleague, teach a cousin to read Quran, or give advice to a friend. Part of you waits for thanks or recognition. {reward}The best reward for good counsel comes from Allah.{/reward}
old: When I help or advise people, I hope for something back.
new: I help for Allah's sake. My real reward is with Him.
try: Help someone today in a way they cannot repay, and do not mention it to anyone.

title: My Lord casts the truth, the Knower of all that is hidden.
subtitle: Revelation sent by the One who sees everything
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {idea}sends the angel with revelation to whom He wills{/idea} of His servants, and He is the Knower of the unseen. Nothing in the heavens or earth is hidden from Him, so His truth is not a guess.
now: Every day you get confident opinions from experts, influencers, and strangers online. Each one sees only part of the picture. {idea}Revelation comes from the One who sees all of it.{/idea}
old: Truth is mostly what the smartest people currently say.
new: Revelation comes from the Knower of the unseen. It weighs more than any opinion.
try: When you face a choice today, look first for what the Quran says before searching opinions.

title: Truth has come. Falsehood can neither begin nor repeat anything.
subtitle: The verse recited at the Ka'bah
then: On the day Makkah was opened, the Prophet ﷺ entered the Sacred Masjid and found idols around the Ka'bah. {idea}He struck them with his bow, reciting: the truth has come and falsehood has vanished{/idea}, and this verse. {trap}Falsehood can create nothing and bring nothing back.{/trap}
now: A lie you told keeps needing more lies to hold it up. A fake image online takes constant effort to maintain. {trap}Falsehood never builds anything that lasts.{/trap} {idea}Truth stands on its own.{/idea}
old: A small lie can hold things together for a while.
new: Falsehood builds nothing lasting. The truth stands by itself.
try: Correct one small untruth you have told, even if it is a little uncomfortable.

title: If I stray, it is mine. If guided, it is His gift.
subtitle: And He is Hearing, Near
then: Ibn Kathir says all good comes from Allah. Ibn Mas'ud, asked about an issue, said: {idea}if I am right it is from Allah, and if wrong it is from me and Shaytan{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}you are not calling one who is deaf or absent, but One who hears, is near, and answers{/reward}.
now: When something goes well, you say: I worked hard. When you mess up: it was bad luck, or my upbringing. {idea}The verse flips it: good is His gift, mistakes are mine.{/idea} And He is near when you call.
old: My successes are mine, and my failures are someone else's fault.
new: My guidance is Allah's gift and my mistakes are mine. He is near when I call.
try: Make a short dua today out loud, remembering He is near and hearing you right now.

title: Terrified, with nowhere to run, seized from close by.
subtitle: No chance of escape on that Day
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: if only you could see the deniers on the Day of Resurrection, {trap}terrified, with nowhere to run and no refuge{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says they will be seized from the first instant. Al-Hasan said this is {trap}when they come out of their graves{/trap}.
now: There are things you run from now: a hard conversation with Allah, a sin you will not look at, a prayer you keep missing. {idea}Today you can still turn and run toward Him.{/idea} That is the mercy of now.
old: I can keep avoiding the hard reckoning with myself for now.
new: There is no running on that Day. Today I can still run toward Allah.
try: Face one thing you have been avoiding with Allah. Talk to Him about it tonight.

title: Now we believe, they say, but faith is out of reach.
subtitle: Belief from too far away
then: On that Day they will say: {trap}we believe in it{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says faith cannot be accepted then, because {idea}the Hereafter is the place of reward, not of testing{/idea}. Like someone reaching for a thing far away, {trap}they cannot grasp it{/trap}.
now: Faith is believing before you see. Anyone will believe once everything is shown. {idea}The value of your faith is that you hold it now, while it is still unseen.{/idea}
old: If I saw proof with my own eyes, then I would really believe.
new: Faith counts because it is held now, before seeing. That is its worth.
try: Renew your faith today: say the shahadah slowly and think about each word.

title: They rejected it before, throwing guesses at the unseen.
subtitle: Poet, sorcerer, madman, just guesses
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}guessed at the unseen{/trap}. Sometimes they called the Prophet ﷺ a poet, sometimes a soothsayer, sorcerer, or madman. Qatadah and Mujahid said {trap}their denial of resurrection, Paradise, and Hell was based on mere conjecture{/trap}.
now: You hear someone say with total confidence: there is nothing after death. Ask what that is based on. {trap}Often it is a guess dressed up as certainty.{/trap} {idea}Your faith rests on revelation, not on a throw in the dark.{/idea}
old: People who deny the afterlife must know something I do not.
new: Denial of the unseen is usually a guess. My faith rests on revelation.
try: Write down three reasons you believe in the Hereafter. Keep them for doubtful days.

title: A barrier between them and what they long for.
subtitle: Doubt that was never resolved
then: Scholars said the barrier blocks what they desire: faith, repentance, and the world they left. Ibn Kathir says both are true. The surah ends on their {trap}grave doubt{/trap}. Qatadah said: {idea}beware of doubt. Whoever dies doubting is raised doubting, and whoever dies certain is raised certain.{/idea}
now: You have a question about faith that has been sitting unanswered for years. You do not ask anyone. You just let it rot quietly. {idea}Doubt left alone does not go away by itself.{/idea} Bring it to Allah and to someone who knows.
old: My doubts can stay in the background. They will sort themselves out.
new: Doubt left alone hardens. I work toward certainty while I still can.
try: Write down one doubt you carry. Ask a trusted, knowledgeable person about it this week.
